dedupe_keys.name: continental us 100 year geomorphic flood susceptibility maps

description: This dataset maps susceptibility to hundred-year river flooding across the continental United States. University of Basilicata and collaborating researchers applied a binary classifier based on the Geomorphic Flood Index to HydroSHEDS elevation data. Eighteen water-resource regions divide the coverage into manageable raster files. The 2017 release supplies georeferenced text rasters at approximately ninety-metre resolution in a ZIP, with NAD83 and UTM Zone 17N stated by the repository. Access is free under the named 4TU General Terms of Use. Coverage is a static terrain-derived classification, not flood observations, water depths or a dated forecast. Terrain resolution and the geomorphic classifier limit interpretation as a detailed hydraulic inundation model. Modellers could use the maps for preliminary infrastructure-exposure simulations or comparisons where local flood maps are missing. data-hydrosheds-hydrorivers-hydrobasins describes the source terrain family, and data-fema-national-flood-hazard-layer provides an official comparison. The file listing and metadata were read without downloading the raster archive.
